issues.legal_issue: The evidence was sufficient to sustain convictions for abetting a suicide where repeated dowry-related harassment and demands were established and the courts below found the accused guilty.
material_facts: The deceased died by suicide after repeated demands for money and harassment by her husband and mother-in-law.
The deceased had recently told her parents that she had been sent to obtain more money and warned that she would not be allowed to live if she did not bring it.
The trial court and High Court found the evidence established the dowry demands and the accused’s guilt.
The Supreme Court found no infirmity in the lower courts’ analysis of the evidence.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 306 of the Indian Penal Code, abetment involves a mental process of instigating or intentionally aiding the commission of the act; a more active role amounting to instigation or intentional aid is required. Courts must assess the evidence and circumstances carefully to determine whether the conduct induced the suicide, and should not find abetment where a person’s hypersensitivity to ordinary domestic discord is the explanation. The Court applied State of West Bengal v. Orilal Jaiswal, AIR 1994 SC 1418, and also set out the definition of dowry in Section 2 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_against_conviction and suicide_established and reliable_evidence_of_repeated_dowry_harassment and recent_threat_or_demand and lower_courts_found_guilt_after_evaluating_evidence

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The accused brought a criminal appeal challenging their convictions for abetting a suicide.
predicates.reliable_evidence_of_repeated_dowry_hara: The deceased’s parents gave evidence of repeated demands for money and harassment connected with those demands.
predicates.recent_threat_or_demand: Shortly before her death, the deceased told her parents that she had been sent to obtain more money and had been warned of dire consequences if she did not do so.
predicates.lower_courts_found_guilt_after_evaluatin: The trial court and appellate court found the accused guilty after considering the evidence.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a conviction for abetting a suicide, suicide is established, reliable evidence shows repeated dowry-related harassment and a recent threat or demand, and the lower courts found guilt after evaluating the evidence, the conviction for abetment is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: The deceased’s failure to disclose harassment to friends and her father’s limited ability to pay did not, by themselves, disprove evidence of dowry demands.
material_facts: The defence relied on the deceased not having disclosed harassment to friends and on the complainant’s limited capacity to pay.
The deceased’s father and mother gave evidence about demands for money and harassment.
The courts below considered the evidence and found that the demands had been established.
issues.conclusion: The absence of disclosures to friends did not positively prove that no dowry demand or harassment occurred, and the father’s limited ability to pay did not prove that no demand was made.
issues.legal_principle: The absence of a victim’s disclosure to friends does not by itself establish the absence of dowry demands or harassment; that circumstance must be weighed with the evidence of the demands. A complainant’s limited ability to pay may affect the assessment of whether payments were made, but does not establish that no demand was made. The Court considered the definition of dowry in Section 2 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_against_conviction and credible_family_evidence_of_dowry_demands and deceased_did_not_disclose_harassment_to_friends and complainant_had_limited_ability_to_pay

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The accused brought a criminal appeal challenging their convictions.
predicates.credible_family_evidence_of_dowry_demand: Family members gave evidence that demands for money and related harassment occurred.
predicates.deceased_did_not_disclose_harassment_to_: The deceased had not told friends about the alleged demands or harassment.
predicates.complainant_had_limited_ability_to_pay: The complainant had limited financial means and said he was unable to meet the demands in full.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal includes credible family evidence of dowry demands, the deceased did not disclose harassment to friends, and the complainant had limited means, those latter circumstances do not disprove the demands.

issues.legal_issue: The custodial sentences could be reduced in light of the peculiar circumstances of the case while leaving the convictions intact.
material_facts: The Court considered the circumstances of the case and reduced the custodial sentence for each appellant.
issues.conclusion: The custodial sentence for each appellant was reduced to three years.
issues.legal_principle: The Court reduced the custodial sentences in view of the peculiar facts of the case; it cited no separate provision or earlier case for that reduction.

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The accused brought a criminal appeal challenging their convictions.
predicates.circumstances_found_to_warrant_leniency: The Court regarded the circumstances of the case as warranting a reduction in custodial sentence.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal results in the conviction being upheld but the circumstances are found to warrant leniency, the custodial sentence is reduced.
